attribution.note: Marcus wrote and endorsed these words in his own Substack post. He co-wrote the linked Fortune essay, but this sentence is his.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his exact figures, his 'roughly' on 150 and his hedge 'nothing that feels like'. It is an observation about current or recent legislative counts.

contract.note: The post names no year and no jurisdiction. The contract reads the figures as 2025 state bills, based on the linked essay he co-wrote. That is an ordinary, fair reading: the figures match the widely cited 2025 tracker totals. A literal reading as a total in May 2026 could differ. The coherence clause is subjective and is rightly left out of the score.

evidence.note: MultiState's dated annual review (Jan 2026) reports 1,208 state AI bills introduced in 2025 and 144 enacted. Both figures match 1,200 and roughly 150.
A dated secondary summary (Feb 2026) reports over 1,200 bills introduced and 145 enacted in 2025. It corroborates the tracker; the one-bill difference in enactments does not matter here.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's reading (US state AI bills in 2025), the tracker's 1,208 introductions and 144–145 enactments match '1,200' and 'roughly 150'. No comparable count contradicts them. Whether nothing 'feels like' a coherent policy is subjective and is not scored. So this verdict covers only the numerical part.
